The answer is C, about -40%. Survey data on school desegregation (NORC and Gallup) show Southern approval far below approval in the rest of the U.S., with the gap widest in the 1950s, at roughly 15% in the South against roughly 55–60% elsewhere. Taking South minus the rest of the U.S. gives a difference of about -40 points. I'm working from memory of those figures, not a source I checked here.

CONFIDENCE: 72
